source.publication: 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions (with the 2025 AR1000F return)
source.section: AR1000F lines 7A-7C, 8-25, 27-29, 34, 37-38 (Form pages 1-2); Instructions PDF page 12 LINE 7A (29 per taxpayer and spouse; 65 or over on January 1, 2026; 65 Special), PDF page 14 Standard Deduction table and LINES 26-29, PDF pages 30-34 Regular Income Tax Table (schedule 0% to 5,600, 2% to 11,200, 3% to 15,990, 3.4% to 26,400, 3.9% above, as settled in the record from the table), PDF page 11 item 8 (Social Security and Railroad Retirement exempt)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (primary) 40,000.00 + wages (spouse) 30,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 38,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). AR1000F, filing status 2 (married filing joint); Arkansas builds its own income from lines 8-25, which here equals federal AGI less the exempt items. Line 8 wages 70,000.00. Line 23 total income = 70,000.00; line 24 adjustments 0.00; line 25 AGI = 70,000.00. Projection check: federal AGI 70,000.00 = state AGI 70,000.00. Line 27 standard deduction (filing status 2) 4,940.00; line 28 net taxable income = 70,000.00 - 4,940.00 = 65,060.00. Line 29 tax, schedule as numbers (0% to 5,600): 2% x (11,200.00 - 5,600.00) 5,600.00 = 112.00 + 3% x (15,990.00 - 11,200.00) 4,790.00 = 143.70 + 3.4% x (26,400.00 - 15,990.00) 10,410.00 = 353.94 + 3.9% x (65,060.00 - 26,400.00) 38,660.00 = 1,507.74; total 2,117.38. (The Regular Income Tax Table row 65,001-65,101 gives 2,117; expected keeps the schedule.) Line 7A boxes: personal 2 = 2 x 29.00 = 58.00; line 7C and line 34 58.00; line 37 total credits 58.00. Line 38 net tax = 2,117.38 - 58.00 = 2,059.38. Status 4 (married filing separately on the same return, PDF page 11 Method A) would tax each spouse on their own income: 40,000.00 - 2,470.00 = 37,530.00, tax 3.9% x 37,530.00 - 419.96 = 1,043.71; 30,000.00 - 2,470.00 = 27,530.00, tax 3.9% x 27,530.00 - 419.96 = 653.71; together 1,697.42 before credits, lower than the joint 2,117.38. The projection taxes status 2 only (approximations); expected follows status 2.
accepted_approximations: Arkansas builds its own income (AR1000F lines 8 to 25) instead of starting from federal AGI; the projection starts from federal AGI less taxable Social Security (exempt) and the reliefs here.

The schedule's bracket starts are derived from the printed tax table, which rounds the tax at each row's midpoint to the dollar; between rows and in rounding the projection's tax differs from the table.

Married couples are taxed on the one table using joint net taxable income (filing status 2). Arkansas also lets them file separately on the same return (status 4, each spouse's tax from the same table on their own income, added), which is lower whenever both have income, because each spouse gets the lower bands.
